items.type: (p : ℕ) → (R : Type u_1) → [inst : CommRing R] → [Invertible ↑p] → ℕ → MvPolynomial ℕ R
items.informal_description: For each natural number $n$, the polynomial $X_n$ is defined recursively as $\left(X_n - \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} p^i \cdot \text{W}_i^{p^{n-i}}\right) \cdot p^{-n}$, where $\text{W}_i$ denotes the Witt polynomial for index $i$, $p$ is an invertible element of the commutative ring $R$, and $p^{-n}$ is its inverse raised to the $n$-th power. items.informal_name: Inverse Jacobian Polynomial in Submersive Presentation
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_3} {σ : Type u_4} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : CommRing S]
  [inst_2 : Algebra R S] [inst_3 : Finite σ] (P : Algebra.SubmersivePresentation R S ι σ) (R₀ : Type u_5)
  [inst_4 : CommRing R₀] [inst_5 : Algebra R₀ R] [inst_6 : Algebra R₀ S] [inst_7 : IsScalarTower R₀ R S]
  [inst_8 : P.HasCoeffs R₀], (MvPolynomial.aeval P.val) (P.invJacobianOfHasCoeffs R₀) = ↑⋯.unit⁻¹
items.informal_description: In a submersive presentation of an $ R $-algebra $ S $ with finite generating set $ \iota $, the inverse of the Jacobian unit $ \operatorname{det}^{-1} $ is expressed as a multivariate polynomial over the base ring $ R_0 $ in the generator variables $ \iota $, demonstrating that this inverse lies in the image of the polynomial map $ R_0[\iota] \to R[\iota] $ induced by the scalar tower $ R_0 \to R \to S $.

items.informal_name: Integer Normalization Preserves Zero Evaluation in Localizations
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (M : Submonoid R) {S : Type u_2} [inst_1 : CommRing S] [inst_2 : Algebra R S]
  [inst_3 : IsLocalization M S] {R' : Type u_3} [inst_4 : CommRing R'] (g : S →+* R') (p : Polynomial S) {x : R'},
  Polynomial.eval₂ g x p = 0 →
    Polynomial.eval₂ (g.comp (algebraMap R S)) x (IsLocalization.integerNormalization M p) = 0
items.informal_description: If a polynomial $ p $ over the localization $ S $ of a commutative ring $ R $ at a submonoid $ M $ evaluates to zero under a ring homomorphism $ g : S \to R' $ at an element $ x \in R' $, then the integer normalization of $ p $, which is a polynomial in $ R[X] $, also evaluates to zero under the composition of $ g $ with the canonical homomorphism $ R \to S $ at the same $ x $.
